thread:
jordan: heads up — after the runtime change rolled last night we're seeing a persistent P99 latency bump on long-context workloads. attached is an nsys capture (s3 link) and a quick screenshot of the timeline. :eyes:

jordan: main symptom: write spikes during kv cache flush/append around token 4800-5200 in big batches. throughput drops ~8% and tail latency increases ~20% on some requests. unsure if kernel selector switched variants mid-batch.

rei: thanks — can you paste the nsys capture command and the runtime config you used? want to repro locally.

jordan: sure — repro command I used locally was:
```bash
nsys profile -t cuda,osrt,cudnn --sample=none -o trace_attn ./run_inference --model gpt-xl --seq-len 8192 --batch 4 --tokens-per-batch 32768
```
runtime flags:
```text
REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS=32768
REDWOOD_ATTEN_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=auto
REDWOOD_KVCACHE_WRITE_BACK=async
```
I attached the nvtx markers around the attention ops in the capture.

amira: quick look — the timeline screenshot shows repeated small kernels named `attention_fused_v2` interleaving with `flash_attn_v1`. that swap pattern can increase SM scheduling churn. did selector heuristics change in the deploy?

jordan: not intentionally. the roll contained a heuristic tweak: prefer fused when avg_seq > 1024 and batch_size >= 2. maybe the avg_seq calculation for mixed-length inputs is off.

perf-bot: regression-detector: ALERT: p99 latency +18% (baseline 72ms -> 85ms) on benchmark long_context_8k after deploy 2026-03-15. top contributor: attention kernel scheduling variance.

soumya: hypothesis: mixed sequence lengths cause the selector to alternate per microbatch. each variant has different shared memory / register usage leading to bank conflicts during kv write-back. also if fused variant uses a different write pattern (coalesced vs strided) the L2/Dram pressure can oscillate.

rei: can you try forcing `REDWOOD_ATTEN_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=flash_only` and rerun the same capture? if the spike goes away that's a strong signal.

jordan: running now on a dev node — will post quick results.

devon: small comment — we saw something similar months ago where the batcher created uneven sub-batches if `max_tokens` permitted splits across different request lengths. patching the batcher to prefer grouping by seq_bucket reduced variance.

jordan: update: ran flash_only capture. early numbers: p99 back to baseline, throughput recovered ~6%. nvtx timeline shows contiguous flash kernels with fewer context switches.

devon: can you paste the snippet from the timeline?

jordan: snippet from the kernel list in nsys (trimmed):
```text
0.000s  attention_flash_attn_v1 (grid 512)  duration 1.8ms
0.002s  kvcache_write_async (grid 64)    duration 0.6ms
0.003s  attention_flash_attn_v1 (grid 520)  duration 1.9ms
0.005s  kvcache_write_async (grid 68)    duration 0.7ms
```
versus the problematic run:
```text
0.000s  attention_fused_v2 (grid 480)    duration 1.6ms
0.0016s attention_flash_attn_v1 (grid 512)  duration 2.0ms
0.0036s kvcache_write_async (grid 128)   duration 1.8ms  <-- big write spike
```

amira: interesting — the fused->flash transition increases the kvcache write grid size in that trace. maybe fused leaves partial writes that flash then consolidates, causing a larger coalesced write later.

soumya: can we get perf counters? sm_efficiency, achieved_occupancy, dram_util, l2_hit_rate for both kernels. small `nvprof`/`nsys` counters snapshot should help.

jordan: grabbed a counters snapshot for both mode runs:
```text
flash_only: sm_efficiency=78% achieved_occupancy=62% dram_util=22% l2_hit=63%
fused_mix:  sm_efficiency=65% achieved_occupancy=58% dram_util=45% l2_hit=37%
```

rei: dram_util + l2 drop in fused_mix = suspicious. more DRAM thrashing and fewer L2 hits. suggests access pattern mismatch.

amira: action plan: 1) short-term: force flash for the scheduled rollout to remove regression; 2) medium-term: add a deterministic grouping pass in the batcher to avoid alternating selector decisions mid-batch; 3) long-term: make the selector aware of kv write footprint (estimate and prefer kernels that minimize write spikes).

devon: re: (2) I can prototype seq_bucket grouping today — will try grouping by nearest power-of-two seq length. low-risk flagged rollout.

jordan: I also reran with `REDWOOD_KVCACHE_WRITE_BACK=sync` to see if async flush contributes. result: tail latency slightly worse, throughput same. so async isn't the root cause.

soumya: thanks — that rules out ordering differences from sync vs async. leaning toward kernel write pattern + mixed selection.

rei: for the grouping patch, please include a lightweight metric in NVTX: `batcher.grouping:bucket=X` so we can verify in traces.

devon: ack — I'll add NVTX spans and a feature flag `batcher.group_by_bucket=true`. will run a canary tomorrow.

jordan: before we close, one more ask: can someone run a perfetto capture on a problematic production trace (redacted ids) and drop the link here? perfetto's CPU<->GPU timeline might show scheduling jitter from the runtime thread that triggers selection changes.

amira: I'll pull one and post later today.

perf-bot: auto-note: created ticket PERF-1873 "batcher grouping to stabilize attention kernel selection" and linked this thread.

jordan: thanks all — good troubleshooting. tagging @engineering-managers for visibility. :thumbsup:

rei: :wave: wrapping up — early mitigation is to pin flash in the next hotfix. I'll open a PR to flip default selector back to prefer flash for now.

soumya: final note — let's collect a small eval that measures kv write amplification (bytes written per logical token) so we can quantify the improvement after grouping.

devon: on it. will post results under the ticket.

amira: great. leaving follow-ups in PERF-1873.

jordan: closing loop here. thanks everyone.
